analyst_view.overall: PSV (3rd, 23 pts) lost 2-1 at home to Club Brugge in the Champions League on Wednesday and have been patchy: they lost at ADO Den Haag and drew with Feyenoord, but beat Willem II 7-0. Cambuur (9th, 15 pts) are unbeaten in six, with 17 scored and 4 conceded, including 6-1, 4-0 and 3-0 wins and a 2-2 draw with AZ. PSV are without Wanner, Lammers, Ouaissa, Pléa, Schouten and Nagalo, and one preview lists Pepi as doubtful.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.6 goals, which assumes a very open game. Cambuur have conceded only 4 in their last six, and PSV have scored below expectation lately (11 in six). PSV are also four days on from a draining Champions League defeat and missing several attackers, so we expect fewer goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. PSV should control the ball, and Cambuur's confident home form doesn't change that picture much.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards. Sander van der Eijk referees, and we found no rivalry or disciplinary angle that moves this.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. Cambuur at home have been attacking freely, and PSV usually shoot a lot, so we see no reason to move off the model.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target. With Lammers, Pléa and Ouaissa out, Pepi doubtful and legs tired after Wednesday, PSV's cutting edge looks blunter than usual against an in-form Cambuur defence.
